sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Gowli appears only in the reproduced Ethnologue genealogical listing (Western Hindi, Unclassified: '.. Chamari, Ghera, Gowli'); no accent data or StressTyp entry for it.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India. Vol. IX, Part I: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group. Specimens of Western Hindi and Pañjābī. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. pp. 550-551 ('Dialects of Central Chhindwara'), 554 ('Gāolī, Rāghōbansī, and Kirārī'), 555 (specimen No. 27, 'Bundēlī (Gāolī), District Chhindwara').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress. p.550: Gaoli etc. 'are all merely impure Bundēlī'; p.554: 'The dialects spoken by them.. in no way differ from the ordinary broken Bundēlī of the district'; pp.551 lists only morphological peculiarities (case signs, pronouns, past of verb substantive); p.555 gives a short Parable specimen with one syntactic remark (agentive with intransitive). The accent remarks elsewhere in the volume (Dakhinī, vernacular Hindōstānī of Meerut, Ḍāngī) do not concern Bundēlī/Gāolī.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank (eds.), Glottolog 5.3, languoid gowl1241 'Gowli' (bookkeeping page and comment)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comment: the Ethnologue entries Gowli [gok] and Gowlan [goj] 'can only match one and the same caste.. on purely linguistic grounds, both are spurious, since the Gowli do not have a language that is mutually unintelligible with all surrounding languages (Grierson 1916: 554-555, Russell and Hiralal 1916)'.

sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 3254.140); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: LSI IX.1 (pp. 550, 554) classes Chhindwara Gaoli as ordinary broken Bundēlī; Jaiswal is the standard phonology of Bundēlī (bund1246) and has an accent section — the nearest first-hand stress description for the variety LSI assigns Gaoli to, though it would be catalogued under bund1246, not gowl1241.
